en: Parivāra 16.
Kathinabheda 1.
Kathinatthata, etc.
For whom is the kaṭhina not spread?
For whom is the kaṭhina spread?
How is it that the kaṭhina is not spread?
In what way is the kaṭhina not spread? For whom is the kaṭhina not spread?
For two types of persons the kaṭhina is not spread.
For one who does not spread [the kaṭhina] and for one who does not express appreciation—
for these two persons, the kaṭhina is not considered spread.
For whom is the kaṭhina considered spread?
The kaṭhina is spread for two persons:
for the one who spreads it and for the one who expresses appreciation.
For these two persons, the kaṭhina is considered spread.
In what way is the kaṭhina not properly spread?
The kaṭhina is not properly spread in twenty-four ways;
it is not properly spread merely by having been scratched.
The kaṭhina is not considered spread merely by washing;
the kaṭhina is not considered spread merely by sorting the robes;
the kaṭhina is not considered spread merely by cutting.
The kaṭhina is not considered formally spread merely by the tying [of the border],
nor is it considered formally spread merely by the making of the *ovaṭṭika* (the inner border),
nor is it considered formally spread merely by the making of the *kaṇḍusaka* (the binding cord).
The kaṭhina is not considered properly spread merely by making it firm,
nor is it considered properly spread merely by making it even,
nor is it considered properly spread merely by making a border around it.
The kaṭhina is not considered properly spread merely by the making of a border;
it is not considered properly spread merely by the softening of the wool;
it is not considered properly spread by means of a sign.
The kaṭhina is not considered properly spread if it is made by means of a formal discourse;
it is not considered properly spread if it is made by means of a fraudulent act;
it is not considered properly spread if it is made from stored goods.
The kaṭhina is not considered spread by means of what is subject to forfeiture;
the kaṭhina is not considered spread by means of what is not formally prepared;
the kaṭhina is not considered spread except by means of a saṅghāṭī robe.
The kaṭhina is not considered spread unless it is done with an upper robe;
the kaṭhina is not considered spread unless it is done with an inner robe;
the kaṭhina is not considered spread unless it is done with five or more than five pieces that have been cut and hemmed on that very day.
The kaṭhina is not considered properly spread unless it is spread by means of a person;
even if the kaṭhina is properly spread, if one expresses the formal appreciation while standing outside the boundary,
the kaṭhina is likewise not considered properly spread.
A "hint" (nimittakamma) means making a sign, thinking:
"I shall spread the Kathina with this cloth.
A "roundabout talk" (parikathā) means making indirect speech.
“By means of this discourse, I shall produce cloth for the kaṭhina.
What is called “storing up” (kukkukata) refers to giving without taking [the gift] into one’s own possession.
There are two kinds of storing up: [storing up by oneself and storing up by others].
Either the presence of the requisite materials or the presence of the stored goods.
"Forfeiture" means that dawn breaks while the act is being performed.
By these twenty-four modes, the kaṭhina is considered not spread.
In what way is the kaṭhina spread? The kaṭhina is spread in seventeen ways:
it is spread with new cloth; it is spread with cloth that is as good as new; it is spread with rags...
The kaṭhina is spread; the kaṭhina is spread with rag-robes; the kaṭhina is spread with shop-ware; the kaṭhina is spread with what is not marked out;
the kaṭhina is spread with what is not formally discussed; the kaṭhina is spread with what is not cut into pieces;
the kaṭhina is spread with what is not stored; the kaṭhina is spread with what is not to be relinquished.
The kaṭhina is spread; the kaṭhina is spread by means of what has been made allowable; the kaṭhina is spread with an outer robe (saṅghāṭī);
the kaṭhina is spread with an upper robe (uttarāsaṅga); the kaṭhina is spread with an inner robe (antaravāsaka);
or the kaṭhina is spread with five or more than five [robes], cut and made into circular patches on that very day.
The kaṭhina is spread for an individual when it has been properly spread;
if the kaṭhina has been properly spread and one standing within the boundary expresses appreciation, then too the kaṭhina is considered spread.
In these seventeen ways, the kaṭhina is spread.
With the spreading of the kaṭhina, how many things arise?
With the spreading of the kaṭhina, fifteen things arise:
eight headings, two obstacles, and five benefits.
With the spreading of the *kaṭhina*, these fifteen things arise.
2. Regarding the *kaṭhina* as an immediate condition (*anantara-paccaya*), etc.:
Which things are conditions by way of immediate condition (*anantara-paccaya*) and equal-and-immediate condition (*samanantara-paccaya*) for the performance?

Is it a condition by way of dependence-condition (*nissaya-paccaya*), a condition by way of strong-dependence-condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*), a condition by way of prenascence-condition (*purejāta-paccaya*), a condition by way of postnascence-condition (*pacchājāta-paccaya*), or a condition by way of conascence-condition (*sahajāta-paccaya*)?
Regarding the preliminary action (*pubbakaraṇa*), which phenomena are conditions by way of proximity-condition (*anantara-paccaya*)? ... [and so on] ...
Which phenomena constitute relinquishing?
… Which phenomena constitute the formal determination?
… Which phenomena constitute the spreading out [of the robe]? …
Regarding the matrices (*mātikā*) and the obstacles (*palibodha*),
which phenomena are related to which basis (*vatthu*) by way of proximity condition (*anantara-paccaya*), contiguity condition (*samanantara-paccaya*),
support condition (*nissaya-paccaya*), decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*), and prenascence condition (*purejāta-paccaya*)?
It is a condition by way of postnascence-condition, it is a condition by way of conascence-condition?
Preliminary effort is a condition for the application by way of proximity-condition, contiguity-condition, support-condition, and decisive-support-condition.
The application is a condition for preliminary effort by way of prenascence-condition.
The preliminary preparation (pubbakaraṇa) is a condition for the performance (payoga) by way of the postnascent condition (pacchājāta-paccaya).
Fifteen states are conditions by way of the co-nascent condition (sahajāta-paccaya).

The relinquishment (paccuddhāra) is a condition for the preliminary preparation by way of the proximity condition (anantara-paccaya), the contiguity condition (samanantara-paccaya), the support condition (nissaya-paccaya), and the decisive support condition (upanissaya-paccaya).
The preliminary action is a condition for the relinquishment by way of the antecedent condition (*purejāta-paccaya*).
The relinquishment is a condition for the preliminary action by way of the post-nascence condition (*pacchājāta-paccaya*).
Fifteen states are conditions by way of the co-nascence condition (*sahajāta-paccaya*).
Resolution is a condition for relinquishment by way of proximity-condition, contiguity-condition, support-condition, and decisive-support-condition.
Relinquishment is a condition for resolution by way of prenascence-condition.
Resolution is a condition for relinquishment by way of postnascence-condition.
Fifteen states are related by way of co-nascence condition.
The four modes of spreading (atthāra) are related to the resolution (adhiṭṭhāna) by way of proximity condition, contiguity condition, support condition, and decisive support condition.
The resolution is related to the spreading by way of prenascence condition.
The eight foundations are related to the performance [of the ritual] by way of the postnascent condition (*pacchājāta-paccaya*).
Fifteen factors are related by way of the co-nascent condition (*sahajāta-paccaya*).

The matrix and the obstacles are related to the performance by way of the proximity condition (*anantara-paccaya*), the immediate-proximity condition (*samanantara-paccaya*), the support condition (*nissaya-paccaya*), and the decisive-support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).
The spreading [of the saṅghāṭi] and the requisites are related to the spreading by way of the pre-arising condition (*purejāta-paccaya*).
Both the requisites and the obstacles are related to the spreading by way of the post-arising condition (*pacchājāta-paccaya*).
Fifteen factors are related by way of the co-arising condition (*sahajāta-paccaya*).
Hope and non-hope are conditions for an object by way of proximity-condition, contiguity-condition, support-condition, and decisive-support-condition.
An object is a condition for hopes and non-hopes by way of prenascence-condition.
Hope and non-hope are conditions for an object by way of postnascence-condition.
Fifteen states are conditions by way of conascence-condition. 3.
Analysis of the Source, Origin, etc., of the Preliminary Task (Pubbakaraṇa).
What is the source of the preliminary task? What is its origin? What is its birth? What is its provenance? What is its equipment? What is its origination?
What is the source of relinquishment? What is its origin? What is its birth? What is its provenance? What is its equipment?
What is its origination? What is the source of the resolve? What is its origin? What is its birth? What is its provenance? What is its equipment?
What is its origination? What is the source of the spreading out? What is its origin? What is its birth? What is its provenance? What is its equipment? What is its origination?
What is the source, what is the origin, what is the birth, what is the production, what is the equipment, and what is the origination of the *mātikā* and the obstacles (*palibodha*)?
What is the source, what is the origin, what is the birth, what is the production, what is the equipment, and what is the origination of hope and lack of hope?

The preliminary performance has application as its source, application as its origin, application as its birth, application as its production, application as its equipment, and application as its origination.

Renunciation has preliminary action as its source, preliminary action as its origin, preliminary action as its birth, preliminary action as its arising, preliminary action as its equipment, and preliminary action as its origination.
Resolution has renunciation as its source, renunciation as its origin, renunciation as its birth, renunciation as its arising, renunciation as its equipment, and renunciation as its origination.
Spreading out has resolution as its source, resolution as its origin, resolution as its birth, resolution as its arising, resolution as its equipment, and resolution as its origination.
The *mātikā* and the impediments have the formal act (*atthāra*) as their source, their origin, their birth, their provenance, their equipment, and their origination.
Hope and lack of hope have the object (*vatthu*) as their source, their origin, their birth, their provenance, their equipment, and their origination.
What is the source of the effort? What is its origin? What is its birth? What is its provenance? What is its equipment? What is its origination?
The preliminary action … [and so on] … the relinquishment … the formal determination …
The introduction … the matrix and the obstacles … the basis …
What is the source, what is the origin, what is the birth, what is the arising, what is the equipment, and what is the origination of hope and hopelessness?
Their application has effort as its source, their origin is in effort, their birth is from effort, their arising is from effort, their equipment is effort, and their origination is effort.
Their prior preparation... [and so on].
Relinquishing … determining … spreading out …
The matrix and the obstacles … the basis … hope and disappointment have their cause and source, their origin, birth, production, accumulation, and manifestation in the cause.
What is the source of the formal act (payoga)? What is its origin? What is its birth? What is its provenance? What is its equipment? What is its origination?
It is prior preparation … [and so on] … relinquishment.
The formal resolution,
the proclamation,
the matrix, and the obstacles.
The basis, as well as hope and disappointment— what is their source, what is their origin, what is their birth, what is their arising, what is their equipment,

and what is their origination? Exertion has conditions as its source, conditions as its origin, conditions as its birth, conditions as its arising, conditions as its equipment, and conditions as its origination.
The preliminary duties … [and so on] … the relinquishing … the formal determination …
The proclamation … the matrix and the obstacles … the basis …
Hope and lack of hope have their root-cause in conditions; they originate from conditions, are born of conditions, arise from conditions, are composed of conditions, and are produced by conditions.
By how many factors is preliminary action comprised?
Preliminary action is comprised by seven factors.
The preliminary task (*pubbakaraṇa*) is comprised of these seven things: washing, examining, cutting, binding, sewing, dyeing, and making it fit.
By how many things is the relinquishing (*paccuddhāra*) comprised?
Relinquishing (paccuddhāra) is comprised of three things:
the outer robe (saṅghāṭī), the upper robe (uttarāsaṅga), and the inner robe (antaravāsaka).
By how many things is formal determination (adhiṭṭhāna) comprised?
The formal resolution (*adhiṭṭhāna*) is comprised of three things:
the outer robe (*saṅghāṭī*), the upper robe (*uttarāsaṅga*), and the inner robe (*antaravāsaka*).
By how many things is the spreading out (*atthāra*) comprised?
The fourfold [set] is comprised by a single factor:
by means of vocal expression.
How many roots does the kaṭhina have? How many bases? How many grounds?
The robe-making ceremony has one root—
the Saṅgha;
it has three bases—
The outer robe, the upper robe, and the inner robe;
the six kinds of cloth:
linen, cotton, silk, wool, hemp, and jute.
What is the beginning of the kaṭhina, what is its middle, and what is its end?
The preliminary preparation for the kaṭhina is the beginning, the formal act is the middle, and the spreading [of the robe] is the end.
With how many factors is a person endowed who is incapable of spreading the kaṭhina?
With how many qualities is a person endowed who is capable of spreading the *kathina*?
With eight qualities is a person endowed who is incapable of spreading the *kathina*.
With eight qualities is a person endowed who is capable of spreading the *kathina*.
Endowed with which eight factors is a person incapable of spreading the *kaṭhina*?

One who does not know the preliminary preparation, does not know the relinquishing, does not know the determination, does not know the spreading, does not know the matrix, does not know the obstacles, does not know the removal,
and does not know the benefits— endowed with these eight factors, a person is incapable of spreading the *kaṭhina*.
Endowed with what eight factors is a person capable of spreading the *kaṭhina*?
He knows the preliminary preparation, he knows the relinquishment, he knows the determination, he knows the spreading, he knows the summary, he knows the obstacles, he knows the removal,
and he knows the benefits— endowed with these eight factors, a person is capable of spreading the *kaṭhina*.
For how many types of persons does the spreading of the *kaṭhina* not take effect?
For how many types of persons does the spreading of the *kaṭhina* take effect?
For three types of persons, the spreading of the *kaṭhina* does not take effect.
The formal act of spreading the kathina robe succeeds for three types of persons.
For which three types of persons does the formal act of spreading the kathina robe not succeed?
One who offers the thanksgiving while standing outside the boundary; one who offers the thanksgiving but does not utter a speech; one who utters a speech but does not make it understood to another.
The formal act of spreading the Kathina robe does not take effect for these three persons.
For which three persons does the formal act of spreading the Kathina robe take effect?
One who is within the boundary boundary-confines the merit; one who, while confining the merit, breaks the silence; and one who, while breaking the silence, makes it known to another.
The formal spreading of the kaṭhina robe is valid for these three types of persons.
How many formal spreadings of the kaṭhina are not valid?
How many formal spreadings of the kaṭhina are valid?
Three ways of spreading the *kathina* cloth do not succeed.
Three ways of spreading the *kathina* cloth do succeed.
Which three ways of spreading the *kathina* cloth do not succeed?
If it is defective in its material, defective in its time, and defective in its execution—
these three kinds of *kathina* spreadings do not take effect.
Which three kinds of *kathina* spreadings do take effect?
If it is endowed with the proper object (*vatthu*), endowed with the proper time (*kāla*), and endowed with the proper performance (*karaṇa*)—these three types of *kaṭhina*-spreading are valid. 4.
The Analysis of What Should Be Known Regarding the *Kaṭhina* and Other Matters.
The kaṭhina must be understood; the spreading of the kaṭhina must be understood; the month for the spreading of the kaṭhina must be understood;

the failure in the spreading of the kaṭhina must be understood; the success in the spreading of the kaṭhina must be understood; the act of designating [a robe] must be understood; indirect speech must be understood;
what is made by stealth must be understood; hoarding must be understood; what is to be relinquished must be understood.
"The Kathina should be understood" means:

the collection, the assemblage, the name, the naming, the designation, the expression, the phrasing, the verbal formulation regarding these very phenomena, namely "Kathina. "The month for the spreading of the Kathina should be understood" means:
[the time for the formal act of spreading the Kathina].
The last month of the rains retreat must be known.
The failure in the spreading of the *kathina* must be known.
Thus, the failure in the spreading of the *kathina* is to be known through twenty-four modes.
"The eighteenfold perfection of the kaṭhina should be known":
the eighteenfold perfection of the kaṭhina should be known by way of seventeen aspects.
"The formal act of designation should be known."
One makes a sign, thinking: "With this cloth, I shall spread the kaṭhina.
One should understand "indirect talk" as follows:
one engages in indirect talk, thinking: "By means of this indirect talk, I shall procure the cloth for the kaṭhina."
"What has been done by oneself" should be understood as not taking [food] by one's own hand;
"storing up" should be understood.
Two kinds of storage should be known: either storage by means of making or storage by means of accumulation.
"It should be known as subject to relinquishment" means that dawn breaks while it is being made.
"The spreading of the *kathina* must be understood:
if cloth for the *kathina* has arisen for the Saṅgha, how should the Saṅgha proceed? How should the one who spreads the *kathina* proceed? How should the one who expresses thanks proceed?

The Saṅgha should grant it to the monk who is to spread the *kathina* by means of a formal act consisting of a motion and a second resolution (*ñattidutiyakamma*). By that one who spreads the *kathina*..."
On that very day, having washed, smoothed, stretched, cut, sewn, dyed,
and made it fit for use, the monk should spread the kaṭhina.
If he wishes to spread the kaṭhina with an outer robe (saṅghāṭī), the old outer robe must be relinquished and the new outer robe formally determined.
The words "I spread the kaṭhina with this outer robe" must be uttered.
If one wishes to spread the kaṭhina with an upper robe, the old upper robe must be relinquished and a new upper robe determined.
The words "I spread the kaṭhina with this upper robe" must be uttered.
If one wishes to spread the kaṭhina with an inner robe, the old inner robe must be relinquished and a new inner robe must be determined upon.
The words "I spread the kaṭhina with this inner robe" must be uttered.

Then that monk who is spreading the kaṭhina, having approached the Saṅgha, having arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, and having extended his joined palms in reverential salutation, should speak to them thus:
“Venerable sir, the kaṭhina has been spread for the Saṅgha; the spreading of the kaṭhina is in accordance with the Dhamma. Please give your thanks.
Those monks who are to give the thanks, having arranged their upper robes over one shoulder and raising their joined palms in reverence, should say this:
“Friend, the kaṭhina has been spread for the Saṅgha; the spreading of the kaṭhina is in accordance with the Dhamma. We give our thanks.”
That monk who has spread the *kathina* should approach several monks, arrange his upper robe over one shoulder, raise his joined palms in salutation, and say to them:
"Venerable sirs, the *kathina* has been spread for the Saṅgha; it is a legitimate spreading of the *kathina*. Please express your appreciation.
Those monks who are to express appreciation should, having arranged their upper robes over one shoulder and raised their joined palms in salutation, say to him:
“Friends, the *kathina* has been spread for the Saṅgha; we rejoice in this lawful spreading of the *kathina*.
Then that monk who has spread the *kathina*, having approached one monk, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, and extended his hands in reverential salutation, should say to him:
“Friend, the *kathina* has been spread for the Saṅgha; this is the lawful spreading of the *kathina*; please express your appreciation.”
That monk who gives the expression of appreciation should arrange his upper robe over one shoulder, raise his joined palms in salutation, and say this:
“Friends, the kaṭhina has been spread for the Saṅgha; the spreading of the kaṭhina is in accordance with the Dhamma; I give my appreciation.
5. The Spreading of the Kaṭhina for an Individual.
"Does the Sangha spread the kathina? Does a group spread the kathina? Does an individual spread the kathina?
"The Sangha does not spread the kathina; a group does not spread the kathina; an individual spreads the kathina.
Since it is the case that the Sangha does not spread the kathina, a group does not spread the kathina, and an individual spreads the kathina...
The kaṭhina has not been spread for the Sangha; the kaṭhina has not been spread for a group; the kaṭhina has been spread for an individual.

Does the Sangha recite the Pātimokkha? Does a group recite the Pātimokkha? Does an individual recite the Pātimokkha? The Sangha does not recite the Pātimokkha; a group does not recite the Pātimokkha; an individual recites the Pātimokkha.
If the Sangha does not recite the Pātimokkha, and a group does not recite the Pātimokkha, but an individual recites the Pātimokkha:

the Pātimokkha has not been recited for the Sangha, the Pātimokkha has not been recited for the group, but the Pātimokkha has been recited for the individual. Through the harmony of the Sangha, through the harmony of the group, and through the recitation by the individual, the Pātimokkha is considered recited for the Sangha, the Pātimokkha is considered recited for the group, and the Pātimokkha is considered recited for the individual.
In the same way, it is not the Sangha that spreads the *kaṭhina*, nor is it a group that spreads the *kaṭhina*; rather, it is an individual who spreads the *kaṭhina*.

Through the Sangha’s expression of appreciation, through the group’s expression of appreciation, and through the individual’s spreading [of the cloth], the *kaṭhina* becomes spread for the Sangha, the *kaṭhina* becomes spread for the group, and the *kaṭhina* becomes spread for the individual.
6. The Exposition of the Questions on Obstacles (*palibodha*)
The removal of the kaṭhina robe is said by the Kinsman of the Sun to be contingent upon departure;
this is what I ask you.
Which obstacle is severed first?
The suspension of the *kaṭhina* robe due to departure was spoken by the Kinsman of the Sun.
And I shall answer this:
first, the impediment of robes is severed;
for him, that occurs simultaneously with going outside the boundary.
The impediment of the residence is severed.
The suspension of the Kathina is declared by the Kinsman of the Sun to be determined by the completion of the work.
And this I ask you:
which obstacle is severed first?
The suspension of the Kathina is determined by the completion of the task.
Thus it was said by the Kinsman of the Sun;
and this I shall explain:
first, the impediment of the dwelling-place is severed.
When the robe is finished, the impediment regarding the robe is severed.
This "conclusion by determination" method for the suspension of the kaṭhina was spoken by the Kinsman of the Sun.
And regarding this I ask you:
which obstacle is severed first?
The lifting of the Kathina occurs at the conclusion of the formal decision.
Thus it was said by the Kinsman of the Sun;
and this I shall explain:
two hindrances are severed neither before nor after one another.
"The suspension of the kaṭhina is said by the Kinsman of the Sun to be non-existent at its end;
this, then, I ask you."
Which obstacle is severed first?
The removal of the Kathina robe by means of its destruction was spoken of by the Kinsman of the Sun.
And this I shall explain to you:
first, the impediment of the residence is severed;
when a robe is lost, the impediment of the robe is severed.
The removal of the kaṭhina at the end of the rains-retreat was spoken by the Kinsman of the Sun;
this, then, I ask you.
Which obstacle is severed first?
The removal of the Kathina robe by means of hearing has been declared by the Kinsman of the Sun.
And this I shall explain to you:
first, the impediment of robes is severed;
upon hearing of that, [it is cut].
The impediment of the residence is severed. This removal of the *kathina* robe, which cuts off expectations,
was spoken by the Kinsman of the Sun.
And regarding this I ask you:
which obstacle is severed first?
The suspension of the Kathina is that which cuts off hope.
Thus it was said by the Kinsman of the Sun:
"And this I shall explain to you:
first, the impediment of the monastery is severed."
When the expectation for a robe is cut off, the impediment regarding the robe is severed.
The removal of the *kathina* at the limit of crossing the boundary was spoken by the Kinsman of the Sun.
And regarding this, I ask you:
which obstacle is severed first?
It is the lifting of the Kathina robe by means of crossing the boundary.
Thus it was said by the Kinsman of the Sun:
"And this I shall explain to you:
first, the impediment of robes is severed."
For him, outside the boundary, the impediment of the residence is severed.
The simultaneous lifting of the *kathina* was spoken by the Kinsman of the Sun.
And regarding this, I ask you:
which obstacle is severed first?
It is the simultaneous lifting of the Kathina cloth.
Thus it was said by the Kinsman of the Sun:
"And this I shall explain to you:
two hindrances are severed neither before nor after."
How many grounds for the suspension of the kaṭhina depend on the Saṅgha?
How many grounds for the suspension of the kaṭhina depend on an individual?
How many grounds for the suspension of the kaṭhina depend neither on the Saṅgha nor on an individual?
One suspension of the kaṭhina depends on the Saṅgha:

the suspension within [the period]. Four suspensions of the kaṭhina depend on individuals: [the suspension due to] going away, [the suspension due to] hearing, [the suspension due to] not hearing, and [the suspension due to] the robe being finished.
There are four terminuses for the kaṭhina: the terminus of departure, the terminus of completion, the terminus of determination, and the terminus of crossing the boundary.
There are four ways of removing the kaṭhina that depend neither on the Saṅgha nor on an individual:
the terminus of loss, the terminus of hearing, the terminus of the cutting off of expectation, and simultaneous removal.
How many modes of suspension of the kaṭhina robe are suspended within the boundary?
How many modes of suspension of the kaṭhina robe are suspended outside the boundary?
How many modes of suspension of the kaṭhina robe may be suspended within the boundary and may be suspended outside the boundary?
Two ways of suspending the kaṭhina robe are suspended within the boundary:
internal suspension and simultaneous suspension.
Three ways of suspending the kaṭhina robe are suspended outside the boundary:
[The robe season ends] with departure, with hearing [the Uposatha], or with crossing the boundary.

There are four ways in which the kaṭhina is suspended: it may be suspended within the boundary, or it may be suspended outside the boundary—namely, by completion, by determination, by loss, or by the cutting off of hope.
How many modes of suspension of the kaṭhina robe have a single arising and a single cessation?
How many modes of suspension of the kaṭhina robe have a single arising and diverse cessations?
Two modes of suspension of the kaṭhina robe have a single arising and a single cessation.
The suspension [of the kaṭhina] by one who has gone inside, and the suspension by all together.
The remaining modes of suspending the kaṭhina arise simultaneously but cease at different times.
The classification of the kaṭhina is finished.
Its summary verse:
"Whose? How? Fifteen;
phenomena, source, and cause."
The compendium of conditions, the roots,
the beginning, the persons for the formal acts,
and the three things— these three should be known.
By means of the spreading out [of the robe], by the recitation,
by the removal of obstacles, by the boundary,
and by the arising and cessation.
